test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 05 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The curved surface area of a right circular cone is 6500π cm², and the diameter of its base is 100 cm. Find the height (in cm) of the cone.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Base **radius (r)** = 100 ÷ 2 = 50 cm.

**Slant height (l)** = CSA ÷ (πr) = 6500π ÷ (50π) = 130 cm.

Using **Pythagorean triplet** (5, 12, 13) scaled by 10 → (50, 120, 130).

Height (h) = 120 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 6500π cm²

**Diameter (d)** = 100 cm ⇒ **Radius (r)** = 50 cm

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area of cone = πrl

Relationship between height (h), radius (r), and slant height (l): l² = r² + h²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/658f4264d65598628b532921a815ce2c35410f01c860a8d583cc52da185efb20.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ π × 50 × l = 6500π

⇒ 50 × l = 6500

⇒ l = 6500 ÷ 50

⇒ l = 130 cm

⇒ h² = l² − r²

⇒ h² = 130² − 50²

⇒ h² = 16900 − 2500

⇒ h² = 14400

⇒ h = √14400 = 120 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 120 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Cone

It is the sum of the curved surface area and the base area: TSA = πr(l + r).

Volume of a Cone

The amount of space occupied by a cone: V = (1/3)πr²h.

Pythagorean Triplets

Standard sets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17) help solve right-triangle geometry problems quickly by scaling.</p
